data.title: Ecthyma — viva
data.summary: Bacterial infections · 16 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Ecthyma** (Bacterial infections)_

**Q1. Define ecthyma.**
- Deep (ulcerative) form of impetigo extending through the epidermis into the dermis, caused by Streptococcus pyogenes ± S. aureus; heals with a scar

**Q2. Who gets it and where?**
- Children and elderly with poor hygiene, malnutrition, diabetes; neglected insect bites, scabies, minor trauma
- Mostly legs and buttocks; soldiers, travellers in hot humid climates, IV drug users, homeless people

**Q3. Describe the lesion.**
- Starts as a vesicopustule on a red base → thick adherent greenish-brown/black crust → removal shows a punched-out shallow ulcer with raised, violaceous, indurated margin
- Usually few lesions; heals slowly over weeks with a scar and pigmentation

**Q4. Differentiate ecthyma from ecthyma gangrenosum.**
- Ecthyma gangrenosum: Pseudomonas aeruginosa septicaemia (rarely local) in neutropenic/immunocompromised patients
- Haemorrhagic vesicle/pustule → painless necrotic ulcer with black eschar and red halo; anogenital and axillary areas
- Histology: bacteria invading vessel walls (necrotising vasculitis without much inflammation) — needs urgent IV antipseudomonal antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam/ceftazidime + aminoglycoside)

**Q5. What is contagious ecthyma (orf)?**
- Not bacterial — a parapoxvirus from sheep and goats; target-like nodule on fingers of handlers; self-limiting in ~6 weeks; may trigger erythema multiforme

**Q6. Give the differential diagnosis.**
- Ecthyma gangrenosum, cutaneous diphtheria (punched-out ulcer with grey membrane), anthrax (painless black eschar with oedema)
- Pyoderma gangrenosum, vasculitic ulcer, sporotrichosis, leishmaniasis, insect bite, PLEVA (multiple crusted lesions), venous ulcer

**Q7. Investigations?**
- Gram stain and culture from under the crust
- Blood sugar; in immunocompromised — blood culture (ecthyma gangrenosum)

**Q8. Treatment?**
- Remove crusts with soaks; topical antiseptic/mupirocin
- Systemic antibiotics for 10 days: cloxacillin, cephalexin, amoxicillin-clavulanate; macrolide if allergic
- Treat the underlying cause (scabies, insect bites); good nutrition and hygiene

**Q9. Complications?**
- Scarring, lymphangitis, cellulitis, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis

**Q10. What is cutaneous diphtheria?**
- Corynebacterium diphtheriae; chronic punched-out ulcer with grey-yellow slough/membrane and rolled edge; may cause myocarditis and neuritis via toxin
- Treat: erythromycin/penicillin + antitoxin if toxigenic; notify; immunise contacts

**Q11. Describe Staphylococcus aureus virulence factors.**
- Surface: protein A (binds IgG Fc), clumping factor, fibronectin-binding proteins, capsule
- Toxins: exfoliative toxins A/B (SSSS, bullous impetigo), superantigens (TSST-1, enterotoxins — toxic shock syndrome, AD flares), PVL (necrotising infections), haemolysins, leukocidins
- Enzymes: coagulase, catalase, hyaluronidase, lipase, staphylokinase, β-lactamase; MRSA — mecA gene (PBP2a)

**Q12. Describe Streptococcus pyogenes virulence factors.**
- M protein (anti-phagocytic; nephritogenic/ rheumatogenic types), hyaluronic acid capsule, streptolysin O and S, streptokinase, DNases, hyaluronidase, pyrogenic exotoxins (SpeA/B/C — scarlet fever, toxic shock-like syndrome), C5a peptidase

**Q13. What is ecthyma gangrenosum workup?**
- Blood cultures, biopsy for histology and tissue culture (Pseudomonas, also Aeromonas, Klebsiella, E. coli, fungi — Aspergillus, Mucor, Fusarium in neutropenia), absolute neutrophil count, HIV; start empirical anti-pseudomonal therapy immediately

**Q14. Ecthyma in India — common settings.**
- Children with scabies/ insect bites and poor hygiene, rural barefoot workers with minor trauma, diabetics, IV drug users; often secondary to pediculosis or scabies — treat the underlying infestation

**Q15. Prevention advice.**
- Treat insect bites and scabies promptly, keep nails short, hygiene, avoid scratching, protective footwear, nutritional support

**Q16. What is pseudomonal hot-foot syndrome?**
- Painful red plantar nodules in children after wading in contaminated pool water (Pseudomonas aeruginosa) — self-limiting; analgesics; antibiotics in severe cases

## Quick spotter facts
- Punched-out ulcer under a thick crust on the leg — ecthyma (heals with scar, unlike impetigo)
- Neutropenic patient + black eschar with red halo — ecthyma gangrenosum (Pseudomonas)

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (ch. Pyodermas); Rook's Textbook of Dermatology for cross-check. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
